content.thinking:
I'm drafting a spec that maps the SOP into rules, with four possible outcomes: surviving spouse, head of household, review, and neither. I'm weighing which outcome should be checked first, since the first matching rule wins, and I'm leaning toward putting review in a position that reflects how unknown facts should be handled.

I'm settling the order of the outcomes: surviving spouse has to come before head of household, since the latter requires the taxpayer not to be a surviving spouse. I'm also considering how to express the "neither" case as a fallback rule, and I'm checking that every numbered section gets accounted for.

Now I'm working through the surviving-spouse conditions: the spouse died within the two preceding years, the taxpayer keeps up the home, a qualifying child lives there all year, and the taxpayer hasn't remarried and no joint return would have been barred.

I'm deciding whether the surviving-spouse outcome should be one rule or several, and I'm settling on a single rule that collects all the conditions, with the sections it draws on cited together.

I'm working out the head-of-household conditions now, starting with the marital-status test: whether the taxpayer counts as married at the close of the year, and whether a legal separation under a decree changes that.

I'm weighing how a spouse who died during the year affects the married-at-close-of-year test. Under 3.2(C) such a spouse counts as married at close of year unless they were a nonresident alien, which would override the home-determined status. The open question is whether that overrides a legal separation under 3.2(A), since the two seem to point in different directions.

I'm checking whether the separation under a decree and the rule that a spouse who died during the year counts as married at close of year pull against each other. I also need to decide whether the section 5 carve-out applies to section 2(b) at all, since section 2(b) doesn't refer to section 7703(b) in this text.

I'm checking whether section 5 can apply to the marital-status test at all, since nothing in the text of 2(b) points to it. The facts I've been given, like whether a separate return was filed, whether the spouse was in the home for the last six months, and whether the child's abode was in the home for over half the year, suggest the drafting expects section 5 to be used anyway, so I'm weighing whether to build that in.

I'm now settling how the head-of-household "not married" condition should be built, weighing the death-of-spouse rule in 3.2(C) against the legal-separation rule in 3.2(A).

I'm writing the section 5 condition into the head-of-household married test: it only applies if the taxpayer files separately, a qualifying child lives in the home over half the year, the taxpayer pays over half the home's cost, and the spouse wasn't in the home for the last six months. I also see that 3.2(C) treats a spouse who died during the year as married at close of year, which seems to conflict with the legal-separation rule in 3.2(A), so the two need reconciling.

I'm weighing the edge case where a spouse dies during the year. Under 3.2(C) that spouse still counts as married at close of year unless they were a nonresident alien, which could override a legal separation under 3.2(A). I'm going to treat the "not married" condition as a combination of these tests, with the death rule carved out as its own exception.

I'm working out how a spouse who died during the year fits into the head-of-household married test: under 3.2(C) that spouse would still count as married unless they were a nonresident alien. So the not-married condition should only hold when the spouse did not die during the year, or the spouse was a nonresident alien. I'm also noting that this may collide with the section 5 carve-out, and I'll leave that conflict visible rather than resolve it.

I'm treating the death-of-spouse rule as a gate on head of household: if the spouse died during the year and wasn't a nonresident alien, the taxpayer counts as married, so that outcome is ruled out. I'm weighing whether to split the head-of-household conditions into separate rules for each path, each repeating the same not-married condition, since there's no way to use a computed fact for it.

I'm settling on a single head-of-household rule and checking which sections feed the marital test, since section 5 may be needed even though 2(b) never points to it. I'm also weighing whether repeating the marital-status condition across separate rules would be cleaner than one combined rule, though the outcomes are what get compared, so either structure works.

I'm weighing how to quote the section texts, since the 5.1 fragment isn't a full sentence, and I'm leaning toward quoting each subsection exactly as it appears. Because rules only lead to outcomes, sections 4 and 5 can't carry their own rules, so I'll point their entries at the head-of-household rule ids instead.

I'm considering a design where the neither outcome is checked earlier, so that the negative marital conditions act as blockers ahead of head of household, and I'm weighing whether that ordering holds up.

I'm weighing whether a default neither rule could sit above head of household, but that would let it override the HoH rule, so I'm keeping the order as review, surviving spouse, head of household, neither, with neither as an empty-condition fallback. I'm also checking whether review needs its own rules, since unknown facts should route there anyway.

I'm deciding the review outcome goes first and has no rules of its own, since unknown facts route there anyway. The surviving-spouse rule being possibly applicable already means review, and the neither default covers everything else. I'm also considering whether to repeat the not-surviving-spouse condition inside the head-of-household rule for clarity, though the ordering already handles it.

I'm settling on a single fallback for the neither outcome, with the review outcome placed first since it has no rules of its own. I'm also weighing whether the persons collection needs a condition, since with no listed persons both the surviving-spouse and head-of-household outcomes would be impossible.

I'm wondering whether an empty list of persons should count as known or unknown, since the persons list is defined as whoever the record presents, and none being presented would mean there are none. I'm still weighing whether a dependent requirement in the SOP would settle that, and I'm leaning toward giving the empty case an explicit rule so a taxpayer with no listed persons can reach the neither outcome.

I'm checking whether an empty list of persons should be treated as known, so a taxpayer with no listed dependents can still reach the neither outcome. The SOP doesn't clearly settle that, and I'm weighing whether a case like a widow with no dependents should default to neither.

I'm deciding which SOP sentence can justify treating an empty list of persons as settled, so a taxpayer with no listed dependents can still reach the neither outcome instead of defaulting to review.

I'm deciding whether an empty list of persons should count as settled, since the list is defined as whoever the record presents and an empty list means none are presented. I'm leaning toward giving the empty case an explicit rule so a taxpayer with no listed persons can still reach the neither outcome. The counts_when condition can be left out, since the list already holds only the persons other than the spouse.

I'm writing the head-of-household path for a taxpayer who maintains a home for a qualifying child, adding the conditions that the child isn't a dependent only because of the 152(d)(2)(H) carve-out and that the taxpayer isn't married at close of year.

I'm checking whether a qualifying child could ever be a dependent only because of the 152(d)(2)(H) carve-out, since that determines whether the dependent-only-by-(d)(2)(H) fact should be a condition on the child path. I'm weighing whether treating it as unknown for qualifying children would send too many cases to review.

I'm checking the qualifying-child path: a qualifying child can't be a dependent only because of the 152(d)(2)(H) carve-out, so that condition should come out as "no" for that person. I'm also wondering whether the "any other person" branch under (A)(ii) should exclude qualifying children.

I'm checking whether a qualifying child who is only a dependent through the 152(d)(2)(H) carve-out could ever reach the other-person branch, and I'm weighing whether to add a not-qualifying-child condition to that path.

Now I'm working through the head-of-household path for a taxpayer who maintains a household that is the principal place of abode of a father or mother, provided the taxpayer is entitled to the section 151 deduction for that parent.

I'm checking the head-of-household path for a taxpayer whose parent's home is the principal abode, and I'm combining the unmarried test as an all-of over two groups: one covering married-at-determination, legal separation, a nonresident spouse, and section 5, and another covering the spouse-died rule in 3.2(C), with the nonresident-spouse exception applied to both. I'm noting that 3.2(C) and the separation rule in 3.2(A) may pull in different directions, so I'll keep that tension visible rather than settle it here.

I'm weighing the priority question between the 3.2(C) death rule and the 5 carve-out. I'll treat the 3.2(C) death rule as a gate and leave the conflict with the legal-separation rule unresolved in the spec.

I'm checking the spouse-died gate against the cases where the taxpayer never had a spouse, which should still pass the not-married test since no spouse died and the marital-status fact is no.

I'm checking the section 5 carve-out for the marital test: it needs the taxpayer married, filing separately, furnishing over half the home's cost, with the spouse absent from the home for the last six months, plus a person in the home.

I'm now splitting the head-of-household rules into separate paths, each sharing the same not-married and case-level conditions, and I'm laying out the section 5 test: married, filing separately, furnishing over half the home's cost, with the spouse absent for the last six months and a child in the home over half the year.

I'm writing out the head-of-household rule as a single structure, with the not-married test and the case-level conditions gating a choice between the qualifying-child path and the other-dependent path. Next I'm laying out the condition for the parent path.

I'm settling the head-of-household path for a taxpayer whose parent's home is their principal abode, requiring the section 151 deduction and that the parent isn't a dependent only through the 152(d)(2)(H) carve-out. I'm also keeping the three head-of-household paths sharing one set of unmarried and case-level conditions, and I'm writing the section 5 test as a fixed structure.

I'm now drafting the three head-of-household rules, deciding how to quote the 3.1 and 4.1 sections, since 4.1 runs long and I'm weighing whether to quote it in full.

I'm checking how the SOP sections on the married-status test and the section 5 carve-out should be cited, including the parts of section 4 and section 5 that still need their text quoted in full.

I'm weighing whether to write the head-of-household rule as one combined rule or three separate ones, since the section 5 and section 4 texts are long and would repeat in each copy. I'm leaning toward a single rule, with the three paths grouped under one set of marital and case-level conditions.

I'm settling on a single head-of-household rule rather than three, since the section 5 and section 4 texts are long and would repeat in each copy. For the neither outcome, I'm working out the wording of its fallback text, and I'm weighing whether the section 1 list item can supply the sentence I quote.

I'm defining the surviving-spouse rule, with the SOP sentences from 2.1 and 2.2 as its source text. Its conditions are a death within the two preceding years, furnishing over half the home's cost, a child who is a dependent and lives there all year, no remarriage, and no nonresident-alien spouse in the year of death.

I'm settling the surviving-spouse rule's order against the head-of-household rule, and I'm listing the outcome set as just the single fallback for neither. I'm checking whether any extra fact is needed to decide whether section 2(b) refers to section 5, since that scope question has no fact of its own in the record.

I'm checking whether section 5 should apply to the marital test in 3.1, since section 2 never points to section 7703(b) and no given fact says it does, so I'll flag that as an open question for the spec's needs list.

Now I'm laying out the section mapping: the neither default takes section 1, the surviving-spouse rule takes 2.1 and 2.2, and the head-of-household rule takes 3.1 through 3.3 along with 4.2 and section 5 and its subsections. Sections 2, 3, and 4 are only headings, so they get no rule of their own, and I'm adding a note on the outcome-setting in 1.1 and on how 4.1 folds into the married-at-determination fact.

I'm drafting the source-text quotes for the persons-list rule, and I'm settling on the first sentences of 2.1 and 3.1 so an empty list is covered.

Now I'm pulling the surviving-spouse text from 2.1 and checking how it lines up with the rule's conditions, and I'm noting that 2.1 also requires the taxpayer to furnish over half the cost of the household.

I'm checking the remarriage and joint-return conditions for the surviving-spouse rule, and then I'm moving on to the head-of-household test that starts in section 3.1.

I'm reading through the head-of-household text in section 3.1 again, checking how the qualifying-child and other-dependent paths are worded, along with the parent path that needs the section 151 deduction.

I'm reading through the rest of the head-of-household rules now, checking the rule that a taxpayer is not treated as head of household if they are a nonresident alien at any point in the year, along with the marital-status exceptions around legal separation and a spouse who died during the year.

I'm going back over the head-of-household text and the section 5 carve-out, since 5.1 cuts off partway through the child-abode condition, and I'm checking which parts of section 5 still need to be accounted for.

I'm pulling in the subsection texts for the head-of-household rule, section 5.1 through 5.4, and I'm planning to join them with ellipses so the quoted sources read as one block. I'm also drafting the unknown-facts note and a review outcome line, along with a neither rule that's still taking shape.

unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be decided on it.

persons.text: For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer- (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151. ... An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either- (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of- (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child- (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151.

rules.text: For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer- (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151. For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual. ... Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse- (A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or (B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien.

An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either- (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of- (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child- (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151. For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual. ... Notwithstanding paragraph (1), (A) an individual who is legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married; (B) a taxpayer shall be considered as not married at the close of his taxable year if at any time during the taxable year his spouse is a nonresident alien; and (C) a taxpayer shall be considered as married at the close of his taxable year if his spouse (other than a spouse described in subparagraph (B)) died during the taxable year. ... Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of this subtitle a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a head of a household- (A) if at any time during the taxable year he is a nonresident alien; or (B) by reason of an individual who would not be a dependent for the taxable year but for subparagraph (H) of section 152(d)(2). ... the determination of whether an individual is married shall be made as of the close of his taxable year; except that if his spouse dies during his taxable year such determination shall be made as of the time of such death; and ... an individual legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married. ... For purposes of those provisions of this title which refer to this subsection, if- ... an individual who is married (within the meaning of subsection (a)) and who files a separate return maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of the taxable year the principal place of abode of a child with respect to whom such individual is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151, ... such individual furnishes over one-half of the cost of maintaining such household during the taxable year, and ... during the last 6 months of the taxable year, such individual's spouse is not a member of such household, ... such individual shall not be considered as married.

Sets the unknowns outcome: a rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to review.
Heading for 2.1 and 2.2. It has no text of its own.
Under 2.2(B), the only bar to a joint return given in the text is a nonresident alien spouse or taxpayer in the year of death.
Heading for 3.1 to 3.3. It has no text of its own.
The order handles the 'is not a surviving spouse' condition: surviving_spouse is ranked above head_of_household.
(C) is written as a gate that applies over (A) and over section 5. The text gives no priority among these 'notwithstanding' clauses.
Heading for 4.1 and 4.2. Its opening words, which say which provisions it applies to, are not in the SOP.
The pack's fact married_at_determination_date already applies the determination date.
